title: IntentEnvelope v2
description: The canonical mutation-proposal envelope adjudicated by @adjudicate/core. Every state-mutating action in an adjudicate-based system crosses the kernel as one of these. The `intentHash` field is content-addressed over (version, kind, payload, nonce, actor, taint, origin) plus `resourceRefs` WHEN PRESENT — see canonical-json-hash.md for the normative algorithm. The `origin` provenance source axis was added in plan 041 (always-present in the pre-image); the OPTIONAL, canonical-drop-safe `resourceRefs` authorization slot was added in plan 031 (bound only when present, so a no-refs envelope hashes identically to its post-041 value). v1 envelopes are REFUSED at runtime with code `schema_version_unsupported`; the only supported version is 2.

version.description: Envelope schema version. Only 2 is currently accepted; v1 envelopes are REFUSED with `schema_version_unsupported` at the kernel's first guard.

kind.description: Domain-defined intent kind (the verb). Pack-specific; e.g. `pix.charge.refund`, `vacation.approve`. The kernel does not validate this string; the Pack's PolicyBundle dispatches on it.

payload.description: Pack-defined payload shape. Opaque to the kernel; passed through to guards. MUST be JSON-serializable. Keys with `undefined` values are filtered before hashing per the canonicalization spec; `null` is preserved.

createdAt.description: ISO-8601 wall-clock timestamp. **Metadata only** — NOT part of the `intentHash` recipe. Adopters can vary `createdAt` freely on retry without affecting dedup. (Pre-T8 the hash included `createdAt`, which silently broke ledger dedup on retry; v2 separates them.)

nonce.description: Adopter-supplied idempotency key. **Load-bearing**: feeds `intentHash`. First attempts pass `crypto.randomUUID()`; retries pass the SAME `nonce` as the original attempt so the ledger can dedupe.

actor.description: Identity of the proposer. The kernel uses `principal` to route auth guards; `sessionId` correlates audit and replay streams.

principal.description: Who is proposing the mutation. Closed enum.

role.description: OPTIONAL, OPAQUE adopter role carrier (WS7). Adopter vocabulary (e.g. OWNER / MANAGER / ATTENDANT) — the kernel assigns it NO meaning and no built-in guard consults it; adopter packs may read it via `envelope.actor.role` for role-aware guards. Orthogonal to BOTH the provenance `principal` axis AND the authority graph's identity binding. Canonical-drop-safe: when absent it is dropped from the `intentHash` pre-image (mirroring `resourceRefs`), so a no-role envelope hashes byte-identically to pre-change envelopes; when present it is bound into `intentHash` via `actor` (tamper-evident). Not in `required` precisely because it is optional/drop-safe.

taint.description: Provenance / trust floor of the envelope. Closed enum forming a lattice: SYSTEM > TRUSTED > UNTRUSTED. The kernel's TaintPolicy gates which intent kinds may execute at each level. LLM-derived envelopes MUST be UNTRUSTED (the framework's load-bearing invariant); webhook-only kinds typically require TRUSTED.

origin.description: Harness-stamped provenance SOURCE axis (plan 041). Orthogonal to `taint`: `taint` is how trusted the content is, `origin` is where the proposal came from. Closed, contaminating enum: Human / Retrieved / ExternalAPI / LLM / System. Part of the `intentHash` pre-image so the LLM cannot post-hoc flip the declared source. In 041 it is stamped and hashed but consulted by NO guard; the propagation gate that reads it is plan 042.

resourceRefs.description: Per-kind resource references (plan 031) — the envelope's authorization slot, a map from a role name (`owner`, `account`, `tenant`, `resource`, …) to the resource identifier the kind operates on. OPTIONAL and **canonical-drop-safe**: when absent (or explicitly undefined) the key is dropped from the `intentHash` pre-image, so a no-resource-refs envelope hashes identically to its post-041 value. When PRESENT it is bound into `intentHash` (so the declared owner is tamper-evident). 031 only adds the slot + hash binding; the authority predicate that reads it is plan 034 and the authority-graph resolver is 032/033 — NO guard consults it in 031. Not in `required` precisely because it is optional/drop-safe.

intentHash.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 over the canonical JSON of the hash-input subset `{version, kind, payload, nonce, actor, taint, origin}` plus `resourceRefs` WHEN PRESENT — note the absence of `createdAt` and `intentHash` itself, and that `resourceRefs` is canonical-dropped when absent (so no-refs envelopes are byte-stable with post-041). See `canonical-json-hash.md` for the normative algorithm and golden vectors. Cross-runtime compatibility (Rust/Go/Python re-implementations) depends on this value being byte-stable across implementations.
